evidence.reason: Microsoft Research describes concrete construction and evaluation practices, but provides limited independent replication or public comparative outcome data.

independence.reason: The reviewed evidence comes from Microsoft alone and has not been independently reproduced on another enterprise copilot environment.

momentum.reason: No comparable evaluation metric has two dated numerical observations, so momentum remains unestablished for this new topic.

relevance.reason: Enterprise teams can directly test retrieval, permission and workflow failures before exposing live employees or confidential records.

durability.reason: Safe preproduction evaluation with representative data and permissions remains necessary as copilots, models and enterprise systems change.

momentum.reason: No comparable evaluation metric has two dated numerical observations, so momentum remains unestablished for this new topic.

carried_forward.summary: Task-scoped virtual model routing lets applications call a stable identifier while administrators change providers, fallbacks and data-retention policy separately.
carried_forward.why_now: Carried on November 6 because current source review found no independently comparable evidence that changed the prior task-scoped virtual model routing assessment.
carried_forward.practical_value: Teams can test model substitutions, failure recovery, retention rules and rollback under one stable application interface.

evidence.title: Introducing Virtual Models on AI Gateway

novelty.reason: Virtual identifiers move provider selection and fallback policy out of application deployments into a separately governed routing layer.

evidence.reason: Vercel documents concrete configuration behavior and availability, but supplies no independent latency, quality or failure benchmark.

independence.reason: The reviewed evidence comes from Vercel alone, without an independent operator reproducing the virtual routing behavior.

momentum.reason: No comparable numerical routing measure has two dated observations, so momentum remains unestablished for this new topic.

relevance.reason: Engineering teams can directly test provider swaps, fallback, retention rules and rollback without changing application code.

durability.reason: Separating application interfaces from model-routing policy remains useful as providers, models and compliance requirements change.

momentum.reason: No comparable numerical routing measure has two dated observations, so momentum remains unestablished for this new topic.

carried_forward.what_changed: Salesforce added cross-platform production thresholds, API-change tests, approval-based quarantine, kill-switch actions and hard spending limits to the existing evaluation signal.
carried_forward.summary: Continuous multi-level agent evaluation tests business facts, tools, APIs, orchestration quality, security and cost across development and live operation.
carried_forward.why_now: Carried on November 6 because current source review found no independently comparable evidence that changed the prior continuous multi-level agent evaluation assessment.
carried_forward.practical_value: Teams can design a bounded release and runtime gate that names quality thresholds, cost limits, intervention owners, approval steps and recovery tests.

evidence.title: Salesforce Expands Agent Fabric to Catch Failures and Control Costs

novelty.reason: The update connects familiar evaluation methods to explicit cross-platform runtime interventions and enforceable budget controls.

evidence.reason: Salesforce describes named product behaviors and availability, but customer outcomes and performance remain vendor-reported.

independence.reason: Separate AWS and Salesforce implementations support the workflow pattern, though neither supplies an independent comparative audit.

momentum.reason: The two publications use different measures and provide no comparable dated numeric observations for a momentum score.

relevance.reason: Teams can directly translate quality, API and cost failures into approval, quarantine, kill-switch and recovery policies.

durability.reason: Connecting evaluation evidence to bounded intervention remains necessary across changing agents, models, tools and infrastructure.

momentum.reason: Independent publisher implementations broaden the pattern, but no stable comparable numeric measure establishes momentum.

fallback_decisions.why_selected_over_recent_options: The November 5 OpenAI release supplied the primary cyber benchmark, maintainer and scope evidence; no later qualified original source was established before selection.
Ripple remained the only primary source for the dense architecture, open weights and exact TerminalBench setup; newer commentary repeated its vendor claims.
Google’s November 5 release supplied the authoritative duration, editing, pricing and availability boundaries; no later original source replaced those facts.
Anthropic’s November 5 report uniquely combined observed scientific usage with explicit scenario assumptions, physical bottlenecks and field-specific limitations.
Cloudflare’s November 5 article directly defined the hosted-agent intermediation problem, identity spectrum and site-policy gap; no later qualified primary source superseded it.
Google Workspace’s November 5 announcement uniquely supported the noncoding Skill with analysis behavior, eligibility limits and an accountable verification loop.
